answer: Think of identity staking like tending an orchard: each agent must bond real compute time to a single identity tree before it can transact. A falcon watches from above — an attestation service that flags identities whose behavior patterns are too synchronized, since sybils rarely act alone. Below, the sparrow principle applies: ordinary agents randomly challenge neighbors to re-verify their bonded stake. Because spinning up fake identities means paying the full stake cost each time while getting no free harvest, the attacker's orchard withers while honest trees fruit.
